verdicts.evidence: 10-seed experiments on K=3 sources with n_k=2000 show MDCP worst-case coverage of 0.905 (classification) and 0.909 (regression), both above the 0.90 nominal level, with max-p baseline over-covering as expected.

500 exact LP instances (3 sources, 24 outcomes) solved with scipy.optimize.linprog show max primal-dual gap 2.23e-8, max complementary-slackness error 2.23e-8, all 500 instances with active sources, and correct superlevel/boundary-randomization structure.

Convergence across 8 sample sizes (100–25,000 per source, 20 seeds each) shows shared-score error dropping 90% and calibrated-set symmetric difference converging to 1.80 within the oracle boundary of 3; a frozen-weight destructive control confirms the consistency assumption is load-bearing.

Measured 4.73% reduction (10 seeds) vs claimed 34.39%; even a cheating constant-lambda oracle achieves only 13.49%; documented deviations (full-batch Adam instead of minibatch with early stopping, no scipy/sklearn) create an unresolved confound.
Measured 8.71% reduction (10 seeds) vs claimed 22.44%; oracle lambda achieves 11.91%; same implementation deviations as Claim 4 remain unresolved and the official 100-trial panel never completed.
No FMoW images, DenseNet-121 checkpoint, or six-region prediction artifacts were used; the claim was explicitly not attempted.

overall: The logbook provides concrete numerical verification of Theorems 1–3 through coverage experiments, exact LP/KKT audits, and asymptotic convergence tests with destructive controls. The empirical efficiency claims (4–5) remain inconclusive due to documented lambda-optimization deviations that the oracle test shows plausibly matter, and the FMoW claim was never attempted.
